title: How to Hire a Startup App Developer (November 2026)
summary: This November 2026 guide walks startups through hiring an app developer, from defining scope to interviewing and tracking candidates.
body_markdown:
Most early-stage teams start an app developer search reactively: a job post goes up in an afternoon, and applications arrive from mobile, web, and backend engineers before anyone has agreed which one the product needs.[How to hire a startup app developer](https://www.dover.com/) comes down to settling the app type, the must-have languages, and the interview stages up front, which can shorten the search and cut down on mismatched hires. That matters when a single engineer carries a large share of a small team’s output, and the sections below follow the process in order, from planning and the job description through sourcing and interviews.


**TLDR:**


- Pick the app type and must-have languages before writing the job description.
- Include a salary range to meet state laws and filter mismatched applicants.
- Mix sourcing channels, such as job boards, referrals, and recruiter support.
- A typical interview runs through a screening call, hiring manager interview, technical interviews, and a virtual onsite.
- Ask candidates how they review and test AI-assisted code.


## Understanding the Role


App developers are experts in coding, but the role calls for more than that. A well-rounded app developer brings creativity and a talent for user experience, and can handle architecture, scalability, bug fixes, and security while staying current on trends and collaborating well with teammates.


App developers often specialize in mobile apps, desktop or web apps, or both. Knowing what kind of app you need built helps you reach candidates with the right skills and programming language knowledge, and it’s a key difference from hiring a standard software engineer.


## App Developer Hiring in 2026


The[BLS software developer outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) projects employment of software developers, QA analysts and testers to grow 10 percent from 2025 to 2035, with roughly 106,100 openings per year across those roles, so startups should expect competition for strong candidates.


AI coding assistants are now common in app development work. The[2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) found that 51 percent of professional developers use AI tools daily, so it helps to ask candidates how they review, test and secure AI-assisted code, alongside the core skills covered below.


## What to Look for in an App Developer


Look for an app developer with technical skill, creativity and the soft skills a growing startup needs. Keep these qualities in mind:


- **Technical proficiency** - They know the programming languages and technologies your app projects require.
- **Problem-solving** - They think on their feet and find practical solutions during development.
- **An eye for UI** - They build apps that feel user-friendly and intuitive to use.
- **Adaptability** - They adjust quickly as tools and priorities shift at a growing startup.
- **Communication skills and teamwork** - They work well within a team and with project stakeholders.


## Planning and Preparation


Before you start hiring, plan and prep first. A clear scope saves time later and keeps your job description from attracting unqualified candidates. If you want a broader view of each hiring stage, our[recruitment process guide](https://www.dover.com/blog/recruitment-process-guide) covers it step by step.


Part of planning is putting your hiring team together, including the hiring manager, future teammates, and any other stakeholders. Once you have your team, align on a few questions to get on the same page:


- What will the day to day responsibilities of the role include, and what team will they join?
- How much experience do they need to be successful in the role?
- What skills do they need? For instance, is the app iOS, Android, both iOS and Android, or desktop? Is the app internal or customer-facing?
- What programming languages are a necessity for the role, and what languages are nice to have but not required?
- What’s the market rate for this position given your size and funding, what’s your budget, and is this a full-time or part-time position?


Once you have a clear understanding of your needs, wants and budget for the role, you and your team are ready to start putting together your job description. It also helps to agree on a few[startup recruiting metrics](https://www.dover.com/blog/recruiting-metrics-for-startups) , such as time to hire, so you can tell whether the process is working as you go.


## Crafting the Perfect Job Description


Crafting the perfect job description is easier said than done, but it’s worth the effort. A great job description will achieve three things:


1. Attract strong candidates for the role
2. Screen out unqualified applicants so you avoid a flood of mismatched applications
3. Communicate your company’s goals and culture so candidates can judge fit


Start by referencing the questions from your planning and prep stage. Be specific about the required skills, experience, and the technologies and programming languages your team uses, describe your startup’s mission and culture, such as your product mission, remote-work policy and team size, and list the perks and benefits candidates care about.


Include a salary range. Pay transparency keeps out applicants expecting far more than your budget allows, saving time for your recruiting team and candidates alike. California, New York, Washington and Colorado already require salary ranges in job postings, per the[pay transparency laws by state](https://www.paycor.com/resource-center/articles/pay-transparency-laws-by-state/) . Virginia’s law took effect July 1, 2026 and Maine’s on July 29, 2026, per Virginia and Maine pay transparency laws, and Connecticut began requiring pay ranges in job ads on October 1, 2026, per[Connecticut’s updated pay transparency law](https://trusaic.com/blog/connecticut-expands-pay-transparency-requirements-effective-october-2026/) , so a remote role may need a range depending on where candidates live.


## Sourcing and Assessing Candidates


Sourcing and assessing candidates is best approached with a mix of strategies. Job boards are one of the most common approaches, and[AI-powered applicant tracking systems](https://www.dover.com/blog/ai-powered-applicant-tracking-systems) can help sort the resulting volume of applicants when paired with clear hiring criteria, though a recruiter or hiring manager should still review the shortlist.


Also, don’t forget to turn to your existing team. Referrals are a fast way to find top candidates, and a good referral program encourages employees to make suggestions for people whose work they already trust.


Another option is bringing in a recruiter when the team’s own bandwidth runs out. An ATS can organize applicants, track stages and support outreach, but someone still has to find passive candidates, run screening calls and keep the pipeline moving, so the decision often comes down to hiring volume and how specialized the role is. Full-time and agency recruiters can be expensive for a growing startup, which is where fractional recruiters through[Dover](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) come in. Each recruiter carries vetted reviews from real hiring teams, so you can check past results before bringing one on. Fractional recruiters can run full-cycle recruiting for a role or take on specific tasks like sourcing or scheduling; for a broader look at flexible people support, see our guide to[fractional HR for startups](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-fractional-hr-a-complete-guide-for-startups) .


## Interviewing Candidates


Once you’ve narrowed down a pool of applicants, a common interview structure for app developers looks like this:


1. **Screening call** - HR or a recruiter confirms the candidate has the necessary qualifications for the role. This stage also offers an early read on whether their personality fits the team.
2. **Hiring manager interview** - Candidates who pass the screening call move to a longer, more in-depth conversation with the hiring manager, covering qualifications, experience, technical skills, and social skills in more detail.
3. **Technical interviews** - This stage puts a candidate’s skills to the test through technical questions, coding exercises, or take-home assessments, and should accurately assess whether they can handle the responsibilities of the role.
4. **Virtual onsite** - A small group of finalists goes through a nearly day-long round of interviews with leadership and cross-functional partners. Interviewers then meet to decide who is the right addition to the company.


*Example app developer interview stages*


Stage Typically run by What it assesses


Screening call HR or a recruiter Necessary qualifications and early culture fit


Hiring manager interview Hiring manager Qualifications, experience, technical and social skills in more depth


Technical interviews Engineering team Coding ability through technical questions, coding exercises and take-home assessments


Virtual onsite Leadership and cross-functional interviewers Behavioral fit and final vetting before a decision

## FAQs


### What skills should a startup app developer have?


Look for technical proficiency in the programming languages your app needs, strong problem-solving, an eye for UI, adaptability and clear communication. At a startup, the ability to own a project from early development through ongoing updates matters just as much as raw coding skill.


### Should I hire a mobile, web or cross-platform app developer?


It depends on what you’re building. App developers often specialize in mobile apps, desktop or web apps, or both, so decide whether your app is iOS, Android, both, or desktop, and whether it’s internal or customer-facing, before you write the job description.


### Do I need to include a salary range in an app developer job posting?


In many cases, yes. States such as California, New York, Washington and Colorado require salary ranges in job postings, and newer laws took effect in 2026 in Virginia (July 1), Maine (July 29) and Connecticut (October 1). A[state pay transparency tracker](https://www.govdocs.com/pay-transparency-laws/) can help you confirm current requirements. Even where it isn’t required, a range helps screen out candidates whose expectations are far above your budget.


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


Not always. An ATS tracks applicants, interview stages and feedback, but someone still has to source candidates, run screens and keep the pipeline moving. A founder hiring one app developer may handle that alone, while a team hiring several engineers at once often adds a fractional recruiter who works inside the existing ATS, so the hiring manager keeps visibility into every candidate.


## Final Thoughts on Hiring a Startup App Developer: Scope, Process, and Support


[How to hire a startup app developer](https://www.dover.com/) comes down to three things: settling the scope before the first posting, building interview stages that test what the role actually requires, and having someone own the pipeline day to day. A team hiring one engineer a year can often run that search itself, while a team hiring several roles at once may find the process stalls without dedicated recruiting time. Dover’s free ATS paired with on-demand fractional recruiters is one way to add that capacity, and the right balance depends on how many roles are open and how much a founder can realistically own.
